question: Does selecting a record for expected information about the historical target beat selecting an unpredictable record after charging acquisition and decoding?
scope: Initial exact supplied-law information ruler: context-current evidence, one purchase, original/wide laws and native/changed execution. This is not a learned policy, law-marginal headroom or architecture-superiority screen.
population: Eight development worlds, 256 matched current episodes per world; no trainable fits or confirmation. Every policy sees the same candidate reports and target cases.

records.operation-event: Truthful record of whether revision preceded repair in this episode, relative acquisition cost 2.
records.contrasting-context: One complete episode with inspection observed, by the same maker, drawn at the current context with its request bit flipped; relative cost 4. Context is externally set and the conditional episode law is normalized within maker/context.
records.noisy-maker-cue: Binary route-preference cue with known reliability .8, relative cost 1. The reported cue, not the true maker identity, is revealed.
records.random-action-distractor: Independent eight-way random-action report with no information about the target, relative cost 1. This tests selection by unpredictable outcomes.

policies.target-information: Choose the largest expected target log-loss reduction minus fee times relative acquisition cost; no purchase wins nonpositive ties.
policies.action-entropy: Choose the largest report-outcome entropy minus fee times relative cost; no purchase wins nonpositive ties.
policies.fixed-cheapest: Always buy the noisy-maker cue, the prespecified choice among equal-cost records.
policies.random: Uniformly choose one of the four reports, using frozen draws shared across fees.

scoring: Uncapped joint log loss, full multiclass Brier, modal accuracy, confident errors, actual target-loss reduction, acquisition cost, net loss (log loss plus fee times relative cost), and loss reduction per acquired cost. Report measured table setup, policy and decoder CPU separately; CPU seconds are not silently converted to log-loss units. Amortize setup over 1/10/100/1000 episodes.
checks: Independent scalar regrouping of every current and conditional historical channel
Separate loop-based joint-outcome entropy and posterior reference
Matched reports across policies and fees
Full frozen scientific replay before acceptance
interpretation: Whole-world paired uncertainty; sampled episodes, policies and fee settings are not independent worlds. Supplied generator law, fixed reliability and same-maker history are privileges. The initial ruler does not establish learnable acquisition, unknown reliability, hidden provenance or sequential complementarity. Native-to-shift contrasts are required; no multiplied-feature reader or duplicated-evidence claim is part of this family.
stopping: Complete the four finite conditions and one full original/native replay once. Retain policy failures. D03/D04/B04/B05 and eligible new-world branches remain independent successors. Do not extend this information ruler merely to fill time.
